RouteStick.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    remaining_path
        When memory is empty and demonstration frames are present, decode all demonstration traversals and write their menu letters in chronological order. Segment at arrivals at adjacent target sites, using highlight changes together with wrist arrival; merge small coordinate fluctuations and temporary double highlights into the same target identity. Preserve every repeated traversal and reversal. Destination x larger than departure x is robot-left, and smaller x is robot-right. Determine the arc from intermediate wrist positions relative to the line joining the wrist resting positions at the departure and arrival sites: image-upper leftward is A, image-lower rightward is B, image-lower leftward is C, and image-upper rightward is D. Do not confuse the wrist with the attached stick endpoint or treat the wrist's offset from target coordinates as evidence of arc direction. Write the full list at this first decision, without deleting the move selected now. On a later decision with carried memory, the intervening execution shows the preceding oracle command completed at its adjacent target; remove exactly one leading letter from the carried list before selecting the next command. The decision-step protocol guarantees that each such return follows one completed command, so do not count individual frames or repeated highlights as additional completions. If there is no intervening completed execution, retain the carried list. Once exhausted, write []. e.g. ["A","B","A","D"]

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    When demonstration frames are present and carried memory is empty, decode the complete demonstrated route according to the policy prompt for memory. Select its first letter as the initial command and write the complete route as remaining_path without removing that letter. The visible demonstration determines this command, not the initial location alone. When carried memory is present, update remaining_path according to the policy prompt for memory, removing the one traversal completed in the intervening execution before selecting the new leading letter. If its first letter is A, select A: move to the nearest robot-left target clockwise. If B, select B: move to the nearest robot-right target clockwise. If C, select C: move to the nearest robot-left target counterclockwise. If D, select D: move to the nearest robot-right target counterclockwise. These conditions apply regardless of the preceding subgoal: after any completed A, B, C, or D, transition to whichever letter now leads remaining_path. The current highlighted target is the departure site, not the destination. Robot-left selects the adjacent target with larger x and robot-right the adjacent target with smaller x; the menu handles these targets internally and requires no point. Never infer the next direction solely from the current location: identical locations can require different moves on repeated visits. If the list is empty, the demonstrated route is complete and no further traversal is intended. Use a location-based fallback only if the demonstrated route is exhausted but a menu answer is nevertheless required, or if the demonstration supplies insufficient evidence to decode the next traversal. Do not use it instead of a traversal supported by the visible demonstration. If fallback is necessary, choose A if a larger-x adjacent target exists, otherwise B if a smaller-x adjacent target exists, otherwise A; this is not an additional demonstrated move.

StopCube.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    passage_count
        Start at 0 for empty memory, otherwise use the incoming passage_count. Process all newly shown observations chronologically, starting with incoming last_side as the preceding side. Compute the sign of cube x minus target x. Each nonzero sign opposite to the preceding nonzero side increments the count once; then update the working side. Ignore exact equality until a nonzero side appears. Include observations during A and B, and count multiple crossings within one decision interval separately. Write the resulting count, without adding any predicted future passage from the command being selected. e.g. 2
    last_side
        The cube's most recently observed nonzero side of the target center, represented as -1 when cube x is smaller than target x and 1 when it is larger. If exactly equal, retain the preceding nonzero side; use 0 if none has yet been observed. Record the side at the decision's final observation, not the side expected after its selected command. e.g. -1
    motion_history
        Maintain an ordered list of observed execution measurements [time, cube_x]; these pairs are not spatial coordinates. With empty memory, start with the initial execution observation. Merge incoming motion_history with all newly shown timestamped execution measurements in chronological order, removing duplicate timestamps. Never include demonstration measurements or predicted positions. Retain all available measurements until observed reversals establish a complete oscillation. Thereafter retain measurements from the first extremum of the latest completed three-extremum sequence (maximum–minimum–maximum or minimum–maximum–minimum) through the current observation, including all intermediate measurements and any motion since that sequence ended. Identify extrema from observed reversals, not an assumed period; for a flat extremum use its last timestamp before reversal. Write this observed history regardless of the command selected. e.g. [[0, 68], [16, 98], [32, 155], [48, 196], [53, 205]]

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    Start in A: move to the top of the visible button to prepare. Select A whenever the hand is not yet in the prepared position. The prepared pose in these observations has the wrist above the button, height approximately 0.15, and closed fingers; do not mistake the wrist's image position for the fingertips' contact point. Determine preparation from the visible pose independently of motion timing: a wrist above the button at approximately 0.15 height with closed fingers is already prepared. Insufficient timing evidence while prepared calls for B, not A. Once prepared, apply the ordinal gate before the timing gate using the updated passage_count, including passages during preparation, and the requested ordinal N from the goal. If fewer than N-1 passages have completed, choose B regardless of proximity or endpoint timing. Only if exactly N-1 have completed should the next-crossing timing estimate determine whether to choose C. C must be initiated before the requested passage because button pressing takes approximately 25–35 recording time units. Select C only when both conditions hold: the updated passage_count equals N-1, and the chronological observations support an estimate that the next target passage is approximately 35 or fewer time units away. N-1 alone never licenses C. If the observations do not establish that the next passage fits within this lead window, select B. Estimate the upcoming arrival from the chronological cube motion shown at this step, first determining whether the cube is approaching or receding from the target and accounting for slowing and reversal at endpoints. When it is receding, estimate the entire time remaining for outward travel, reversal, and return to the target; do not use distance divided by speed as though it were approaching. Select B if that complete trip exceeds the lead window or the observations do not establish that it fits within it. Slowing outward motion alone is not evidence that pressing is timely. Estimate timing using incoming motion_history combined chronologically with all newly shown timestamped execution measurements, removing duplicate timestamps. Do not restrict the estimate to the current interval when retained observations supply earlier motion. A useful estimate fits smooth periodic motion x(t)=a+b*cos(w*t)+c*sin(w*t) to this accumulated evidence and finds the next crossing of the currently visible target x after the final observation. Measure the remaining time from that final observation. When accumulated observations establish a repeatable period T, directly check the crossing estimate using historical phase: identify an observed crossing of the visible target in the direction of the upcoming passage, interpolating its time between bracketing measurements as needed. Advance that crossing time by whole periods to its earliest recurrence after the final observation, and subtract the final observation's time. Use the direction of the upcoming crossing, including any intervening reversal, rather than automatically using the most recently completed crossing, which may have the opposite direction. This historical-phase calculation can establish timing alongside the smooth periodic fit; it is not a requirement when a sufficiently sampled partial cycle already supports the estimate. The fit must explain the accumulated observed trajectory, not merely the latest low velocity. A sufficiently sampled partial cycle showing acceleration followed by deceleration toward the opposite endpoint can support a periodic fit and next-crossing estimate even before a reversal is observed. Observed reversals or a complete oscillation strengthen the estimate but are not prerequisites. Do not assume a period or extrapolate a near-zero endpoint velocity as constant. Use the fitted motion to include any remaining outward travel, reversal, and return to the target. If the accumulated observations do not adequately constrain the next crossing to approximately 35 or fewer time units after the final observation, select B; otherwise select C only if the updated passage_count equals N-1. Outward slowing or reaching an endpoint alone does not establish that the next crossing fits within the lead window. An endpoint turnaround can already be the press-launch time for a fast cube if a supported periodic-motion estimate places the next crossing within the lead window and the updated passage_count equals N-1. Moving toward the target is not required for C; a supported estimate of the complete time to the next crossing is required. At an endpoint, low instantaneous speed or the absence of a newly observed reversal does not invalidate a next-crossing estimate already supported by retained motion history. After updating passage_count from all newly shown observations, choose C when that count equals N-1 and the supported historical-phase or periodic-fit estimate places the next crossing within approximately 35 time units. Apply the uncertainty fallback only when the accumulated evidence genuinely leaves timing underconstrained, not merely because the current observation is at an endpoint. Select B while fewer than N-1 passages have completed, or while the requested next passage remains farther away than this lead window. Reevaluate after every B; remaining static can span several passages, so update memory from every shown frame. None of these menu options requires a supplied point; A and C concern the visible button. If motion timing is uncertain, default to B while refining the estimate from the next observations, rather than pressing on the wrong ordinal. If already stopped at the requested target, remain static. For other uncovered situations, prepare with A if necessary, otherwise remain static with B.
